subject: Banking
title: Proprietary Trading
description: A quick win: understand Proprietary Trading.

hook.text: Before 2010, investment banks traded billions of their own money in markets.

buildup.text: Proprietary trading means the bank bets its own capital on stocks, bonds, currencies, and derivatives for profit.

discovery.text: Prop traders used the bank's cheap funding and market information to gain an edge over regular investors.

twist.text: The Volcker Rule in 2010 banned most prop trading at banks. The risk was too high.

climax.text: Prop trading was the most profitable and dangerous activity in banking. Regulation killed it to protect the system.

punchline.text: $10 billion from trading. Too profitable and too dangerous. Now banned.

quiz.question: What did the Volcker Rule do?
options: Banned most proprietary trading at banks to reduce systemic risk
